applicableAreas: Southern property boundary near trees proposed in clearance-restricted zone
findings.comment: Proposed trees measured at 0.5 feet and 4 feet from overhead electric distribution conductor (southern boundary). Non-utility-compatible trees must maintain 15-foot lateral clearance from distribution conductors. Cedar Elm and Live Oak, among the proposed species, are not typically utility-compatible per ECM Appendix F criteria. Clearance violations are evident from measured distances alone.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary near trees proposed in clearance-restricted zone
findings.comment: Large trees (Cedar Elm ~50-60 ft, Live Oak ~50-80 ft mature height—both exceeding the 40-foot threshold per ECM Appendix F) are proposed at 0.5 feet and 4 feet from the overhead electric distribution conductor. Large trees require 25-foot lateral clearance from distribution conductors. Violations confirmed by field measurements.

applicableAreas: Southern, western, and eastern property boundaries where overhead electric poles are shown
findings.comment: Utility poles associated with overhead electric lines are shown on the electrical design plan (Sheet 21) at multiple locations on the site perimeter. Trees proposed within 10 lateral feet of utility poles are prohibited. Although poles are depicted on the electrical plan, specific locations and distances from proposed trees cannot be verified from the landscape plan without explicit dimension callouts.

applicableAreas: Areas near Buildings 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, and 7 where transformer pads are shown
findings.comment: Electrical transformer pads are located near multiple buildings on the site (per electrical plan, Sheet 21). Trees proposed within 10 lateral feet of pad-mounted equipment or between access doors and drivable surfaces are prohibited. Specific pad locations and tree positions relative to pad access doors cannot be verified without explicit dimension callouts on the landscape plan.

applicableAreas: Areas where pull boxes, electrical meters, and underground electrical vaults are proposed
findings.comment: Multiple electrical pull boxes, vaults, and underground utilities are shown on the electrical design plan. Trees proposed within 5 lateral feet of underground electric equipment are prohibited. Specific equipment locations and distances from proposed trees cannot be verified from the landscape plan without explicit dimension callouts.

applicableAreas: Areas where trees are proposed within 20 feet of underground electrical equipment
findings.comment: No root barrier specifications, details, or notes are evident on the landscape plan (Sheet 31) or landscape details sheet (Sheet 37). Trees proposed within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment require root barriers minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment. Absence of these details prevents verification of compliance.

applicableAreas: Areas near overhead electric facilities where large trees (40+ ft mature height) are proposed
findings.comment: Large trees (Cedar Elm ~50-60 ft, Live Oak ~50-80 ft mature heights) are proposed on the site but are not visually differentiated on the landscape plan itself. While plant schedules (Sheet 35) contain mature height data, this information is not called out or symbolized on the landscape plan drawing to allow field personnel to readily identify which plantings are large trees subject to the 25-foot clearance requirement from distribution conductors.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where overhead electric line is shown
findings.comment: No dimension lines, distance callouts, or measurement notes are shown on the landscape plan indicating how clearances from the overhead electric conductor were determined. Clearances must be measured from the outer (outside) conductor position, not from the utility pole centerline. Without documented measurement methodology on the plans, compliance cannot be verified.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where overhead electric line is shown
findings.comment: No dimension lines or measurement callouts on the landscape plan indicate the measurement reference point (tree trunk center versus canopy edge). All clearance measurements must originate from the tree trunk (planting location), not from the projected canopy edge. Without explicit documentation of measurement methodology, compliance cannot be verified.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where trees are proposed within restricted clearance zones from overhead electric conductor
findings.comment: Trees are proposed at 0.5 feet and 4 feet from the overhead electric distribution conductor, within the prohibited clearance zones (15 feet for non-utility-compatible trees, 25 feet for large trees). No documented written approval from Austin Energy authorizing these plantings in restricted zones was found in the supplementary documents. The Master Comment Report identifies Austin Energy tree/landscape clearance requirements (UCM § 1.10.10.3 & 4) as pending review.
